title: the-owner-is-a-database-and-every-link-is-a-tuple
owner: db_domain owns the schema and the store (charter gated_by CC; codemother owns the care of the code, ruling 2026-09-06). CC/Opus builds. Akien owns the design already made: a database per owner, now.
intention: Every durable leaf has the address <owner>.<table>.<leaf>, the owner segment IS a Postgres database of that owner's own, every link is a tuple of two addresses readable from both ends, and the fixed lists (embeddings, blobs, records) are positional, void-and-reuse, never deleted.
why: Akien's vision, recorded whole 2026-09-06 at CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/I-the-vision-that-guides-every-decision.md: a household and a lab with several principals and one Igor serving all of them, so 'the problem of who owns what takes on a new dimension'. Ruled the same day: 'the per owner database is a thing we do before things become even more complicated.' Measured the same day: cairn_links holds 0 rows, so the link tuple has no installed base to retrofit; every day after the cast it grows one.
traces_to: Law 6 (ownership in the address, and the owner's gate is now a database boundary, which is physics per Law 4); Law 1 (provenance derived from the link structure, never re-derived); telos 3 (share those tools with others: the vision's household and lab need several principals). falsifier.proves_red: DONE when, on this box: (1) `psql -l` lists cairn_librarian, cairn_codemother, cairn_inference_domain and cairn_bus, and the migrated row counts equal the source counts measured 2026-09-06 (cairn_nodes 10,538; cairn_embeddings 11,230; librarian_nodes 148; codemother_root_nodes 47); (2) address.parse/render round-trips every address in a fixture set including file addresses with env vars; (3) a write to a librarian table through connect('codemother') is refused, loudly; (4) a link written from owner A to owner B appears in both link tables, and after A voids its row, links_to(B's address) still names A's row from B's side, so nothing orphans; (5) void then allocate on an embeddings list reuses the voided row id; (6) grep finds no `dbname=` and no DB_NAME outside store.py; test_db_domain.py, test_sole_path.py and the librarian's tree proofs stay green after migration. WRONG INTENT if a consumer turns out to need a cross-owner SQL join (the design says links are addresses the store resolves, never joins), or if one box for one person needs more than one Postgres role to run.

questions.a: Three named. (1) 'database (per owner)' means a Postgres database — load-bearing; chosen because a database is the unit that takes its own credentials and moves hosts whole, which is what the household and lab use case needs; the wrong-intent tooth (a needed cross-owner join) is the measurement that would overturn it. (2) The role Cairn runs as has CREATEDB — true today, ensure_database already creates `cairn` with it; one box, one role stays the bound. (3) A link between two owners written as two half-rows stays consistent without a distributed transaction — held because each half is owned and gated by its own side and the reverse traversal reads locally; a half that fails to write is a loud OwnershipError, never a silent orphan.

Two points were asserted wrapped and are not. (a) What happens to the old `cairn` database after migration: it becomes read-only and stays until the scratch-tables ticket drops it; nothing writes there after the crossing, and the proof's grep tooth (no DB_NAME outside store.py) is what makes that true. (b) The clearance (read gate) is NOT wrapped and is deliberately out: the ticket lands the one seam it will sit on (store.read(address) across owners) and says so, rather than inventing a permission model the vision has not specified.

Consulted the lab (recompiled 2026-09-06 after the vision intention). Law 6 served, not collided: the owner's gate becomes a database boundary. 'One master db' (six-box swarm, memory one-bus-per-cairn-instance): a distinction, per-owner databases live in one instance's Postgres; recorded in the intent. 'Inter-device queries via bus verbs': the one real edge, recorded on the ticket as a question for Akien, one function's seam, not a build blocker. Idea 2026-09-06 scratch-tables census: sibling, its drop is its own ticket. No decision or intention in the lab says one database.

A Haiku-level builder needs: (a) WHERE — cairn/devices/db_domain/address.py (new), store.py (connect(owner), ensure_database(owner), registry per database, read(address), links_to/links_from, void/allocate), migrate_to_per_owner.py (new, copy migrate_to_three_tables.py's shape); (b) THE NAME RULE — owner `x` is database `cairn_x`, identifier-safe lowercase, no other prefix; a table inside it carries no owner prefix (cairn_nodes becomes cairn_librarian.nodes); (c) THE LINK ROW — columns local text, remote text, kind text, weight real, traversals integer default 0, created timestamptz default now(); unique(local, remote); index on remote; write both halves, each through its owner's connection; (d) THE LIST ROW — integer row id as the address leaf, `voided boolean default false`; allocate = lowest voided or next; (e) ORDER OF WORK — address.py with its proof first; then store.connect(owner) with test_db_domain.py green against `cairn_test`; then links and lists with their teeth; then move trees.py (NODES_TABLE, EMBEDDINGS_TABLE, LINKS_TABLE, THREADS_TABLE, OWNER='librarian'), bus.py (_BUS_OWNER), inference_domain/domain.py (CACHE_OWNER) and codemother's root table onto connect(owner); then run the migration and assert the counts; (f) DON'TS — no cross-database join, no second connection path (test_sole_path.py stays the tooth), no dropping the old database (that is the scratch ticket), no read gate invented here, no change to the write-gate semantics (non-owner refused, unregistered refused, where-less refused).

constraints: No cross-database SQL join, ever: a link is two addresses the store resolves.
db_domain stays the sole connection path (test_sole_path.py is the tooth).
No read gate (clearance) invented here; the ticket lands the one seam it will sit on and names it.
Write-gate semantics unchanged: non-owner refused, unregistered refused, where-less refused.

Ownership model confirmed by Akien ('exactly yes'): an employer delegates access to an employee. Each principal (Akien, CC, an Igor, the librarian, each device) holds its own creds; per-owner database is what a credential is for.

Until the hardening step before sharing, the librarian is allowed access to everything ('for now, the librarian is just allowed access to everything'). The migration and store.read(address) may rely on that; nothing may assume the read gate is closed.

The old `cairn` database IS dropped in this voyage, after the migration's count assertions pass: ticket 201a37bf1613 sweeps its 9,075 scratch tables out first, so nothing but the twelve live tables remains to copy (amended 2026-09-06 by CC under the delegated ordering; the earlier line assigned the drop to the scratch ticket).
how: db_domain grows the address, the per-owner database and the link tuple in one voyage; the librarian, bus, inference_domain and codemother callers move onto them; a migration carries the live rows across and leaves the old `cairn` database read-only. (1) ADDRESS: db_domain/address.py parses and renders `<owner>.<table>.<leaf>`; file-side addresses are `file:<path>` with env vars allowed. (2) PER-OWNER DATABASE: store.connect(owner) reaches Postgres database `cairn_<owner>`, created on first touch the way ensure_database creates `cairn` today; DB_NAME retires; the owner registry (`cairn_owned`, CHECK owner <> '') lives inside each owner's database and records that owner's tables, so a write to owner B's table through connect(A) is refused by the database boundary before the registry ever looks. Reads of another owner's address go through store.read(address), which opens that owner's database; this is the seam a clearance (read gate) lands on later, and it is the only cross-owner route (db_domain is the ruled exception to no-cross-device-imports). (3) LINK TUPLE: each owner's database carries `links` with local, remote, kind, weight, traversals, created, unique(local, remote), indexed on remote; a link between two owners is written in both owners' tables, each side writing its own half, so Law 6 holds and reverse traversal (links_to(address)) is a local read on either side. (4) LISTS: embeddings, blobs and records carry integer row ids with a `voided` flag; void(address) flips it and returns the reverse links; allocate(table) reuses the lowest voided row. (5) MIGRATION: db_domain/migrate_to_per_owner.py, shaped like the librarian's migrate_to_three_tables.py, copies the twelve registered system tables to their owners' databases (cairn_nodes/embeddings/links/threads and librarian_nodes to cairn_librarian; codemother_root_nodes to cairn_codemother; inference_calls to cairn_inference_domain; bus_traffic and its delivery table to cairn_bus), asserts the row counts, and leaves the 9,075 scratch tables in the old database for the scratch-tables ticket to drop.

intent.what: Every durable leaf has the address <owner>.<table>.<leaf>, the owner segment IS a Postgres database of that owner's own, every link is a tuple of two addresses readable from both ends, and the fixed lists (embeddings, blobs, records) are positional, void-and-reuse, never deleted.

challenge.better_approach: A Postgres SCHEMA per owner inside one database would give `<owner>.<table>` names natively and keep cross-owner joins possible. Rejected here because the vision's unit is the principal: a database is what gets its own credentials (a clearance) and moves to another host whole; a schema is neither. The sketch says database, and the ruling says now. Keeping one database and adding an owner column was the cheapest shape and is what exists today (cairn_owned, 94% scratch entries): it makes ownership a lookup, which the intention names as the thing to invert.
challenge.prior_art: store.py: ensure_database/connect/_ensure_registry/create_owned_table (the owner-gate to generalize); trees.py §6.2 link()/_ensure_links with LINKS_TABLE=cairn_links (built 2026-08, 0 rows on 2026-09-06, so the tuple has no installed base to retrofit); migrate_to_three_tables.py (the migration shape); the addressing intention's two-species table; idea 2026-09-06 scratch-tables census (sibling, the drop of the old database's 9,075 scratch tables is its ticket, not this one's).
challenge.hidden_assumption: That 'database (per owner)' in the sketch means a Postgres database, not a schema or a prefix. Load-bearing and named; the falsifier's wrong-intent tooth (a needed cross-owner join) is what would show it wrong. Second: that every owner in the system is a principal worth a database. The bus and inference_domain are devices, not household members; they get one because the rule admits no exemption (a singleton is instance 0, never a special case), and because a device that moves hosts takes its database with it.
challenge.real_collision: Memory 'one bus per cairn instance ... one master db': the six-box swarm ran once on one master database. A distinction, not a collision: per-owner databases still sit in one instance's Postgres; multi-host is an address resolution change, and the owner segment is what makes it one. Memory 'inter-device queries via bus verbs': device A asks device B through a verb, not through B's tables. Distinction recorded as an open edge on the ticket: a cross-owner address resolve is db_domain reading B's database directly today (the ruled exception), and whether it should instead ride a bus verb is Akien's call, not a build blocker; the seam is one function.

why_beneath_the_why: Akien 2026-09-06: 'we're not trying to build all that today, but this is the vision i carry that guides every decision i make.' The owner in the address is what lets Leah's things, an Igor's things and Akien's things sit in one system without one of them owning the others.
filed_edges: RESOLVED by Akien 2026-09-06 (ruling 2026-09-06-the-employer-delegates-access-and-the-librarian-administers-it): a cross-owner read is a permission on the store, not a bus verb. 'as an igor's employer, i would give him access to my db. and then the librarian would set up the permissions for that as the overall owner.' The seam stays store.read(address); the permission it will check is administered by the librarian and granted by the employer through the vault (idea 2026-09-06-each-user-me-you-igor-etc-has). This ticket still builds no read gate; it lands the seam.
